about: How the Conferbot web widget runs a bot flow, node type by node type: what it reads, shows, accepts, stores and which handle it leaves by. Generated by scripts/parity/flows/gen.js from spec.src.js; every cite is file:line under the dev folder (conferbot-widget, client, embed-server). The fixtures in fixtures/ are the executable half: they were run through the widget's own code.

source.widget: conferbot-widget/src (index.ts engine, ts/chat/displayStep.ts display, ts/chat/handlers/* answers, ts/chat/richNodes*.ts rich steps, ts/chat/flowControl*.ts loops/sub-flows)
source.server: embed-server/src/utils/widgetFlow.js (secrets stripped from node data before the widget sees it)
source.realData: samples/real-nodes.json (export.js, read-only, local only - never committed): data keys and handles as saved in a real database; customer nodes anonymised (anon.js)

flowShape.rule: The flow is chatbot.elements[0].nodes and chatbot.elements[0].edges. Node = {id, type, data, position...}; edge = {id, source, sourceHandle?, target, targetHandle, type:"customedge"}. sourceHandle may be missing or null on old edges.

secrets.rule: The server strips apiKey / api_key / openaiApiKey from every node and sets gpt-node data.serverSideAi = true. An SDK must never need a secret from node data (GPT, AI and payment calls go through the server).

start.rule: The chat starts at the FIRST node with type "welcome-node" in nodes[] (not nodes[0], not a node without incoming edges). Its data.text is the first transcript line. No welcome-node: the widget throws and shows nothing.

next.rule: A step that does not branch moves on along the FIRST edge in edges[] whose source is the step, ignoring sourceHandle. The edge is pushed to the record. No such edge, or its target node does not exist: the chat ENDS. The second edge is never tried.

port.rule: A branching step leaves by an exact handle: the edge with source === step id AND sourceHandle === handle (string equality; no prefix/suffix matching, no "source-1" vs "1"). No such edge: the chat ENDS - never another edge, never the next node in the array. A wired edge whose target node is missing makes the widget throw (nextNode.type) and the chat stops where it is.

richPortFallback.rule: Rich steps leave through goPort(handle, fallback): the handle when it is wired; else the fallback when ONLY the fallback is wired; else the handle (which ends the chat). Steps with no fallback end the chat on an unwired outcome.

end.rule: Ending: if a sub-flow call is open, return to it (flowControl.returnFromSubflowPath) instead. Otherwise hasChatEnded = true, the record is sent, socket "chat-flow-completed" {chatSessionId} is emitted and the post-chat rating popup opens 1500 ms later.

unknownNode.rule: A node type the widget does not dispatch (a newer builder step, or real-data types like ask-custom-node, go-to-step-node, time-out-node, business-hours-choice-node, zoho-node) is passed: hidden-fields/loop/sub-flow steps run first if it is one; otherwise console.warn, nothing is shown, and on the next tick the flow continues along the unknown node's FIRST edge (engine.next). No edge: the chat ends. A welcome-node reached mid-flow is not a display step and is passed the same way.

dispatch.rule: Entering a node: it is pushed to steps[] and to the record (_nodeRecord: node + renderedText + time). Display types (core/node-processors/nodeTypeCategories.ts DISPLAY_NODE_TYPES, which includes the rich steps) are drawn after the typing dots and then categorised (transcript line + answer-variable placeholder). Logic, integration and special types run their handler directly. Everything else is unknownNode.

answerVariables.rule: answerVariables is a list of {nodeId, key, value}. A question step with data.answerVariable registers {nodeId: node.id, key, value: null} when it is SHOWN; its answer then fills the entry by nodeId (_setAnswerVariable updates only an existing entry). A step without data.answerVariable stores nothing (the answer is still in the record and transcript). Legacy v1 steps never register a variable. Logic / rich extras are saved BY NAME (saveVariableByName: update every entry with that key, else add one; nodeId "column_mapped_<key>" when none is given). Reading {key} uses the FIRST entry with that key.

masking.rule: Unless customizations.redactSensitive === false, values stored as variables and the text fields of visitor record entries are masked (card numbers, IBANs, ids, passwords -> "[card •••• 4242]"); the entry gets redacted: ["card"]. The transcript keeps what was typed.

interpolation.rule: Bot text is filled from the answer variables before it is shown: {x}, ${x}, {{x}}, ${ANSWERS.x} and $${x} (a literal "$" then the value). Keys are \w+ (letters, digits, _). An unknown, null or "" value shows NOTHING and the gap is tidied ("Hey ${name}, welcome" -> "Hey, welcome"; "Hi {name} there" -> "Hi there"; a lone "{name}" paragraph disappears). Values are HTML-escaped; a list reads "a, b"; a matrix answer "Row: Col · Row2: Col2"; other objects JSON. Applies to every prompt and option label drawn through parsedHtmlElement and to renderedText; NOT to image/video/audio/file URLs; html-node fills raw then sanitises; redirect/navigate links fill with URL-encoding in the query. Stored answers are the raw option text (a choice labelled "Yes, {plan}" is saved as "Yes, {plan}").

typing.rule: Every displayed step shows typing dots first, for paceFor(previous step, this step, previousWasAutoAdvance) ms. len(step) = data.text ?? questionText ?? calendarPrompt ?? message, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed. After the visitor answered (or the first step): clamp(500 + len*12, 700, 1800). Right after an auto-advance step (welcome, message, image, video, audio, file, html, user-redirect): clamp(len(previous)*22, 350, 2200) + clamp(250 + len*6, 300, 900). A message whose text is blank HTML, or an image with an empty data.image, is skipped with no dots. Logic/integration steps show nothing and take no time unless stated.

composer.rule: Typed text is trimmed; an empty send is ignored. Routing by the waiting step: user-input-node, user-range-node, ask-multiple-questions-node, human-handover-node (pre-chat / post-chat / live), else the ask-question handler (which first offers it to a waiting AI / KB step).

validationErrors.rule: A refused answer shows a message (above the composer, or as a bot bubble) and the step keeps waiting; nothing is recorded. Rich cards show their error inside the card.

records.rule: Every visitor answer is pushed to the record (sent as socket "response-record") with id = the step id and a shape such as "user-selected-choice"; an entry with the same id AND type|shape is merged, a different shape is its own entry. The transcript [{by:"bot"|"user", message}] gets the step's RAW prompt (not interpolated) and the visitor's answer.

handles.source: the single exit of a step (builder default), also success / found / verified / paid paths of rich steps
handles.source-<n>: legacy numbered exits: two/three-choices (source-1..3), user-range (source-1 below, -2 within, -3 above), quiz (source-1 wrong, source-2 right), condition / boolean / business-hours (source-0 true|open, source-1 false|closed), rating-choice (source-<value-1>), opinion-scale (source-<value-from>), random-flow legacy (source-<index>)
handles.source-<id>: n-choices (choice.id), image-choice (image.id), yes-or-no (option.id), carousel / product-card (button.id), random-flow (branch.id), ai-route (intent.id)
handles.source-failed: otp not verified, payment failed or cancelled
handles.source-fallback: ai-route: no intent (or an intent with no edge)
handles.source-error: run-subflow: sub-flow missing, too deep, or recursive
